newsitem.title: USA: Navajo 750 MW coal-fired unit seen up Thurs night.
newsitem.headline: Navajo 750 MW coal-fired unit seen up Thurs night.

text.p: The 750 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Navajo power plant near Page, Ariz., was expected to be back up Thursday night, sources familiar with the plant's operations said early Thursday.
The unit has been down since Tuesday for repairs to a boiler tube.
Navajo's other two 750 MW units were said to be operating normally.
The Navajo plant is operated by Salt River Project, which also holds a 21.8 percent equity stake in the plant.
Other owners include the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, Arizona Public Service Co, Nevada Power Co and Tucson Electric Power Co.
